query: Casting is the predominant fabrication method for high-entropy alloys, but solidification-related porosity and microstructural nonuniformity can cause heterogeneous properties. Studies of other high-entropy-alloy compositions have reported high hardness and notable compressive performance, yet these findings do not establish how to improve CoCrFeNiTi; moreover, some investigated alloys were brittle at 25 °C and displayed only limited plastic deformation at 600 °C. For equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi with a simple crystal structure, favorable plasticity and machinability, but low hardness and load-bearing capability, what single intervention could improve hardness and mechanical performance while preserving those favorable characteristics and clarifying the relationship between microstructure and deformation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, a quantitative prediction relative to the unmodified alloy, the processing and testing boundaries within which it should apply, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled microstructural and mechanical experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a specific amount of nano-sized precipitates, such as Mn₂O₃, into the CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy through a controlled processing technique, such as selective laser melting (SLM) or mechanical alloying, will improve its hardness and mechanical performance while preserving its favorable plasticity and machinability.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with a simple crystal structure
generation.intervention: Introduction of nano-sized precipitates, such as Mn₂O₃, through controlled processing techniques like SLM or mechanical alloying
generation.conditions: Processing conditions such as temperature, pressure, and atmosphere control during SLM or mechanical alloying
generation.structural_mediator: Nano-sized precipitates, such as Mn₂O₃, and their distribution within the alloy matrix
generation.mechanism: Orowan strengthening and grain boundary strengthening due to the presence of nano-sized precipitates, leading to improved hardness and mechanical performance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved hardness and mechanical performance, including yield strength and compressive strength, while maintaining favorable plasticity and machinability
generation.baseline: Unmodified CoCrFeNiTi high-entropy alloy with a simple crystal structure
generation.boundary: Processing conditions, such as temperature and pressure, and alloy composition
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount and distribution of nano-sized precipitates, as well as the specific processing conditions, required to achieve the desired improvement in hardness and mechanical performance

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled experiment with varying amounts of nano-sized precipitates and processing conditions to evaluate the effect on hardness and mechanical performance
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of nano-sized precipitates does not lead to a significant improvement in hardness and mechanical performance, the hypothesis is falsified

Question: What are the temperature-dependent mechanical properties and deformation mechanisms of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy additively manufactured by selective laser melting (SLM) compared to conventionally processed alloys?. System: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Selective laser melting (SLM) using pre-alloyed spherical powder (average diameter 27.2 µm); laser power 90 W, scan speed 600 mm/s, hatch space 80 µm, layer thickness 25 µm, volumetric energy density 75 J/mm³, 180° rotation scanning pattern, high-purity Ar atmosphere.. Test conditions: Compression tests at 25, 500, 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C; initial strain rate 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹; engineering strain limit 0.4; specimens preheated at 10 °C/min; MoS₂ lubricant used.. Question: How can a nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film with superior mechanical and tribological properties be synthesized using a cost-effective single target, and what are the effects of annealing on its adhesion and wear performance?. System: Equimolar CuMoTaWV refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film deposited on silicon and 304 stainless-steel substrates. Processing: DC-magnetron sputtering using a single target prepared by partial spark plasma sintering (SPS) of equimolar elemental powders (Cu, Mo, Ta, W, V) at 1000 °C under 40 MPa pressure; film deposition at 500 °C substrate temperature for 120 min in Ar atmosphere (1.16 × 10⁻³ mPa, 150 W power); post-deposition annealing at 300 °C for adhesion improvement. Test conditions: Nanoindentation at 3 mN load; nanopillar compression (440 nm diameter, 3 mN max force); tribological wear tests at room temperature (RT) and 300 °C with 1 N load and 0.1 m/s sliding speed against E52100 alloy steel counterballs. Question: How can high-throughput computational screening be used to discover lightweight, precipitation-strengthened high-entropy alloys with high-temperature strength superior to traditional ferritic superalloys?. System: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system (specifically Al20Cr5Fe50Mn20Ti5 and Al15Cr5Fe50Mn25Ti5 as successful cases). Processing: Arc-melting of 99.9 wt% purity constituent elements, melted at least six times for homogeneity, followed by drop-casting; subsequent homogenization at 1200 °C and annealing at 700 °C for 2 hours for specific characterizations. Test conditions: Compression tests at room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 700 °C) at a strain rate of 2 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; in situ neutron scattering from room temperature to 1050 °C; synchrotron XRD and TEM characterization.
